speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for your patience. To begin our evaluation, could you describe the specific onset and progression of your gait and limb ataxia? Additionally, do you have any known history of autoimmune disorders, diabetes, or prior strokes?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. Since the ataxia is prominent on the right side, have you noticed any specific triggers like heat exposure, or any recent infections or tick bites? Additionally, do you have any history of Lyme disease, syphilis, or unexplained weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. Given your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab and the new onset of unilateral ataxia, PML is the most likely diagnosis. I am requesting an MRI of your brain to confirm the presence of non-enhancing white matter lesions.
